columns.label: Ebook
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily get and consume ebooks on the platform (free or paid) as a first-class product, open, buy, borrow, or read without hunting.

columns.label: Short-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily consume short-form video as a first-class surface (For You, Reels, Shorts).

columns.label: Long-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch creator / UGC long-form video (or specialty long video) as a core surface. Course lectures belong under Courses. Hollywood catalogs belong under Series/Films.

columns.label: Series/Films
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch series and films as an SVOD / catalog entertainment product.

columns.label: Courses
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily take or browse structured courses as a first-class product.

columns.label: Newsletters
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily read or subscribe to newsletters / creator writing as a first-class product.

columns.label: Audio
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily listen to music, podcasts, or audiobooks as a first-class product.

columns.label: Memberships
columns.definition: Yes if a creator or seller can accept payments from others and make money through the platform, checkout, fan subscriptions, tips, ads, shop, or creator funds. Not only a classic Patreon-style membership product.

columns.label: Community & Messaging
columns.definition: Yes if you can create or join a group, community, or club, including group chats, Groups, subreddits, community tabs, discussion boards, or community feeds. A one-off comment on a single video or listing is not the bar; a durable place for the group to talk is.

columns.label: Storefronts
columns.definition: Yes if the product gives a creator a custom storefront or site that can take the place of building their own website (bio page, creator site, branded shop). Not a shop tab on someone else’s multi-seller marketplace.

columns.label: Marketplaces
columns.definition: Yes if a typical person can search and shop a catalog of offerings from many sellers, courses, books, digital goods, etc. Storefront software (Shopify, WooCommerce) is not a marketplace unless shoppers browse many sellers there.

scaleFacts: Targets non-technical creators (coaches, course creators, consultants) with integrated storefront and business tools.

Modules include link-in-bio store, digital products & courses, coaching & sessions, memberships & communities, email & automations, client CRM + chat, and payments/payouts (including splits and subscriptions).

strengths.title: Complete digital business hub
strengths.detail: Storefront, scheduling, memberships, courses, CRM, chat, and email, minimal tech overhead for solo creators.

strengths.title: Strong link-in-bio store
strengths.detail: Professional, premium-looking landing pages for selling from bio.

strengths.title: Native coaching and sessions
strengths.detail: Built-in booking, video calls, and session management, often replaces Calendly-style tools.

strengths.title: Memberships and communities
strengths.detail: Recurring subscriptions and private member areas, good for coaches running programs.

weaknesses.title: Younger platform with smaller ecosystem
weaknesses.detail: Less known than Podia, Kajabi, or established storefronts; fewer integrations, tutorials, and community support.

weaknesses.title: Depth vs breadth trade-offs
weaknesses.detail: As a broad all-in-one, some features (advanced courses, complex funnels) may be weaker than specialized tools.

weaknesses.title: Potential lock-in
weaknesses.detail: Running the whole business on Pensight can make migrating later more complex.

content:
Kahana is a library of curated hubs, Explore, Clubs, and optional Stripe. Pensight is link-in-bio, landing pages, or creator storefronts. They overlap in places and diverge in others.

What each one is

Kahana is built around hubs people can open, Explore so strangers can find them, Aura as scarce daily recognition, and Clubs so discussion outlives a feed. Selling stays optional.

Pensight is a powerful all-in-one creator platform that serves as a complete digital business hub, for solopreneurs with shared knowledge, built-in playbooks, and an AI teammate.

Why this comparison

This article puts Kahana and Pensight side by side. It covers what each supports as a first-class product job, key features, and a few research notes so you have a clearer picture of what they are, how they compare, and what you can actually do on each one. It is not a teardown, and it is not a switch-tomorrow pitch.
contentAfter:
What you can do on each

On Kahana you can publish a hub, list it on Explore, discuss it in a Club, grant Aura, and turn on a Stripe paywall when you are ready to charge.

On Pensight you can use Memberships and Storefronts as first-class product jobs. You only need a door: route followers to many tools, or a thin storefront you already know.

Using Kahana with Pensight

You can use both. Pensight keeps doing what it already does well. Kahana is another place to package the work, get discovered, and grow an audience.

Keep Pensight as the door that routes followers to many tools. Add Kahana as what they open: a profile and hubs, listed on Explore, with optional paywalls. Put Kahana as the main learn or buy link on Pensight so the bio is not twelve exits and no room behind them.
